text:
Jordan: Hey team — ACME Health POC kickoff. They want Private deployment access. Question from sales: should we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink for the POC? They have strict egress controls.
Alia: TL;DR — PrivateLink for strict security/no overlapping CIDR; VPC peering if low latency and no CIDR overlap. We should confirm CIDRs and whether they allow interface endpoints.
Sam: Quick network check: do they have overlapping CIDRs with our Private deployment ranges? If yes -> PrivateLink only. If no -> peering is simpler. @acme-ops can you confirm your CIDR blocks?
acme-ops: We run 10.0.0.0/16 in their non-prod account and prod is 10.1.0.0/16 — no overlap. Prefer peering to avoid extra ENIs.
Tash: For peering we'll need route table entries on the subnets used by their app and ours. Also security groups to allow 443 (control plane) and 8443 (inference). We'll provide exact ports.
Jordan: They also asked whether model downloads during provisioning require outbound internet / NAT.
Sam: Options: 1) Use a NAT Gateway from their VPC to reach S3/model registry; 2) We stage the model in a customer-controlled S3 bucket with cross-account read; 3) For air-gapped POCs we can supply a model bundle for on-prem install. Which option do they prefer?
acme-ops: Prefer staging in our S3 (cross-account read). What's needed from us?
Alia: We'll need their AWS account ID, VPC ID, list of private subnet IDs, route table IDs, and an IAM role ARN that allows our infra to read the staging bucket (or we can provide presigned URLs for the model objects during the POC).
acme-ops: Got it. One more: how do Hosted API keys map to Private deployment? They want to test with existing app using hosted keys over the peering link.
Tash: Hosted API keys cannot be routed into customer VPCs. For Private deployment you get a customer-only endpoint (DNS inside their VPC) and separate auth tokens. For POC we can issue temporary tokens scoped to the env. We'll exchange tokens via secure CDK or SSM parameter with customer-managed KMS.
Jordan: Can eng drop a minimal terraform snippet for peering + route example for their devops team? They asked for a copy/pasteable example.
Sam: Sure, here's a minimal example — adjust CIDRs and IDs:
```
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "redwood_acme" {
  peer_vpc_id   = "vpc-ACME"
  vpc_id        = "vpc-REDCLOUD"
  peer_owner_id = "123456789012"
}
resource "aws_route" "to_redwood" {
  route_table_id             = "rtb-EXAMPLE"
  destination_cidr_block     = "10.2.0.0/16"
  vpc_peering_connection_id  = aws_vpc_peering_connection.redwood_acme.id
}
```
Sam: You'll also need the reciprocal route on ACME's side. Security group example: allow outbound 443/8443 to Redwood subnets.
acme-ops: Perfect. Also need sample language for security questionnaire fields: "Where are keys stored?" and "Who has access?"
Alia: Short answers we can provide: "Keys stored in KMS-managed key stores, customer keys can be used for Private deployments; access is limited to customer-nominated admins and Redwood infra service accounts for provisioning. We can provide SOC2 report and one-page security summary for the POC."
Tash: Note on performance: if they want low-latency inference, best to place Redwood Dedicated pool in same AZs as their subnets. We'll need AZ mapping from ACME to pin capacity.
Jordan: Next steps: ACME to send CIDRs + account ID + subnet IDs + preferred model staging option by EOD tomorrow. Engineering to draft minimal terraform + a 1-page security QA doc and temp-token process. I'll loop in pricing for a 30-day POC after we have AZs.
acme-ops: Acknowledged — we'll send the details by EOD. Thanks all!
